questions.stem: A student reacts calcium carbonate with hydrochloric acid in an open beaker and observes that the mass decreases. Why does the mass appear to decrease?

options.text: Some atoms are destroyed during the reaction
The acid evaporates during the reaction
Carbon dioxide gas is produced and escapes into the air
The calcium carbonate dissolves and loses mass

questions.explanation: The reaction produces carbon dioxide gas (CaCO₃ + 2HCl → CaCl₂ + H₂O + CO₂). In an open beaker, the CO₂ escapes into the air, so the measured mass of the beaker and its contents decreases. Mass is still conserved overall — the gas has simply left the system.

questions.stem: 24 g of magnesium reacts completely with 16 g of oxygen. According to the law of conservation of mass, what mass of magnesium oxide is produced?
questions.explanation: The law of conservation of mass states that the total mass of reactants equals the total mass of products. Therefore, mass of MgO = 24 g + 16 g = 40 g. No atoms are created or destroyed — they are simply rearranged.
